pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Values - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
‘Love your neighbour as yourself’Luke 10:25-37
Chapmanslade School is a truly unique village school. Pupils consistently demonstrate and show a passion for being good neighbours. Our Christian vision, to ‘love your neighbour as yourself’ comes from Luke 10:25-37, The Parable of the Good Samaritan.
Our school is an inclusive place where every member of our school community shows compassion and service, looking out for each other. We recognise all of our pupils as individuals, celebrating their strengths and differences. We aim to give courage to our pupils to achieve their full potential, experience personal successes and thrive in all that they do. We focus on relationships and building trust; modelling this to our wonderful young learners.
We believe that these are the core values shown by the good Samaritan in the parable and in the hymn, ‘When I Needed a Neighbour, Were You There?’.
Recognising its historic foundation, Chapmanslade School will honour and protect its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England, working in partnership with Chapmanslade and Corsley Churches and the Salisbury Diocese. Chapmanslade School serves its community by providing an education of the highest quality within the context of Christian belief and practice, encouraging an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith, and promoting Christian values through the experience it offers to all its pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values & Equality - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values & Equality
We are very proud that our school has been awarded both the Widening Inclusivity In Religious Education [WIRE] & Gold WIRE awards for our work related to inclusivity and understanding other religions and cultures.
British Values
The Department for Education has published guidance to schools on promoting British values to prepare young people for life in modern Britain.
We teach and support the fundamental British values of:
These values are embedded throughout our school vision and values, our curriculum, Collective Worship and daily school life.
Pupils at Chapmanslade live these values everyday through our school vision of loving your neighbour. Our school rules: Ready, Respectful and Safe also help pupils in championing British Values, especially in treating everyone equally and kindly.
We talk about these values every day through Collective Worship, PSHE, Religion & Worldvies lessons as well as in other subjects.
We use the Jigsaw PSHE scheme which also specifically promotes the fundamental British values. Jigsaw contributes to the British Values agenda very significantly, both through the direct teaching of information and through the experiential learning children will enjoy.
Democracy
The Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Mutual Respect and Tolerance
Equality
Through always trying to be a good neighbour, we promote that:
The Equality Act became law in 2010. It covers everyone in Britain and protects people from discrimination, harassment and victimisation - everyone in Britain is protected. This is because the Equality Act protects people against discrimination because of the protected characteristics that we all have. Under the Equality Act, there are nine Protected Characteristics:
Within our Collective Worship, and curriculum (most notably our carefully chosen text selection), we teach about and promote protected characteristics in our curriculum and embed them into our entire ethos. Our school vision and school values enable us to ensure children understand and show compassion, service, courage and trust toward all of our neighbours.
Everyone is different
We celebrate our differences
We are all equal in our differences
Disability
Gender reassignment
Religion or belief
Marriage or civil partnership
Sexual orientation

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
We celebrate our love of God through participating in daily Collective Worship in school.
This year’s Christian Values are Thankfulness, Trust, Perseverance, Justice, Service & Truthfulness. We follow a two year rotation of values, working closely with our clergy and church, St Philip and St James’. Where possible, we take joy in holding services in the church for our pupils and parents.
Come to us with light O God, Be with us this day.
We hold a daily Collective Worship in school, including regular reflection time focused on our current Christian Value. We model windows, mirrors and doors thinking, encouraging our pupils to look outwards at the world, reflect back on our lives and act – do something because of what they have learned.
Mondays: Mr Cottrell’s Collective Worship
Tuesdays: Teacher Lead Collective Worship
Wednesdays: Class-Based Collective Worship
Thursdays: Local Clergy members’ Collective Worship
Fridays: Reflective Collective Worship on current Christian Value
We also hold an additional Celebration Assembly on Fridays.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome from the Headteacher
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Chapmanslade Church of England Primary School. Nestled in the heart of our village, our school is more than just a place of learning—it's a vibrant, caring community where every child is valued, nurtured, and inspired to achieve their full potential.
As a small village school, we pride ourselves on our close-knit community and the strong relationships we build with our families. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to create a supportive and stimulating environment where children feel safe, happy, and motivated to learn. Guided by our Christian ethos—“Love your neighbour as yourself”—we encourage our pupils to become kind, responsible individuals, ready to meet the world with confidence and compassion.
We are proud of our school's achievements and the positive feedback we receive from families and visitors. Our most recent Ofsted inspection (March 2023) reaffirmed our status as a ‘Good’ school. Our subsequent SIAMS inspection (October 2024) was extremely positive. Both inspections praised the dedication of our team and the enthusiasm of our children.
If you are considering Chapmanslade for your child, I invite you to explore our prospectus here to learn more about our curriculum, values, and daily life at the school. Should you have any questions or wish to arrange a visit, please don’t hesitate to get in touch - we would love to welcome you in person and show you what makes our school so special.
Please contact Mrs McCall (morning) or Mrs Coughlin (afternoon) in the school office on 01373 832367 or email us at admin@chapmanslade.wilts.sch.uk for all enquiries.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Music Performance 2026 - News - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pupil Music Performance 2026
Celebratory Music Performance in Church
We celebrated pupils' musical talents in church with a service dedicated to just music.
When we visit church for services, we always give several pupils the opportunity to demonstrate their talents; welcoming in our parents prior to the services beginning. This has become ever more popular, with more and more pupils performing. For the first time, this July, we held a dedicated service in church to celebrate music within our school.
We heard performances from several pianists, guitarists, a drummer, our recorder group, choir and KS2 pupils also performed several songs from the recent Fairy Queen Opera Project (see news).
It was a wonderful, well-attended celebration and lovely to welcome parents to share more of our creative side. Staff were incredibly proud of everyone who performed. We definitely plan to make this an annual event!

pageCache.pageTitle: KS2 Join Fairy Queen Opera Project - News - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
KS2 Join Fairy Queen Opera Project
We have been offered the opportunity for our Key Stage 2 pupils to take part in a performance of the opera ‘The Fairy Queen: Three Wishes’ at the Wiltshire Music Centre in Bradford-on-Avon. Our pupils will join a children’s chorus of around 150 children to perform alongside the world-class baroque orchestra The Orchestra of the Age of Enlightenment, professional opera singers, and a band of musicians from St Laurence school.
The project kicked off on 18th May when visiting musicians ran a workshop/rehearsal in school. They will visit one more time in Term 6, and on the morning of 30th June we will travel to Bradford-on-Avon for a final rehearsal and performance (all taking place within the school day).
This is a very special chance to work alongside professional musicians, improve our singing technique, explore baroque and modern music together, and experience participating in a full-scale performance. We can't wait!
Update - 30th June 2026 Performance
The whole of Key Stage 2 went on a visit to Wiltshire Music Centre for a performance of the opera 'The Fairy Queen'. The stage was filled with performers: musicians from the Orchestra of the Age of Enlightenment, students from St Laurence school band, a conductor, and 4 incredible singers, dressed in amazing costumes and performing a hilarious story! But we weren't just watching the performance: we were a big part of it! We have been practising hard in school, with our teachers and with visiting musicians, to prepare ten songs that were part of the show. The performance was amazing and it was a memorable experience to sing our hearts out as part of a huge choir. Well done to all of the pupils involved!

pageCache.pageTitle: KS1 West Wiltshire Dance Festival - News - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
KS1 West Wiltshire Dance Festival
Pupils from our KS1 Dance Festival Club performed at Bath Forum!
A group of pupils from Years 1 and 2 travelled to Bath Forum with teachers to participate in the West Wiltshire Dance Festival. The theme for this year's dances was books. Throughout the afternoon, they took part in several workshops including a rehearsal for their performance; a cinema workshop; a mindfulness/yoga session; a games session; and a creative booklet session.
Later on, parents and family came to watch all of the pupils' performances on the (big!) stage at Bath Forum. Our school's dance was based on 'Room on the Broom' by Julia Donaldson. Dancing to the Witch Doctor', we had great fun with our energetic and catchy routine!
We can't wait for next year's performance already!

pageCache.pageTitle: Redwood Class visit Bristol Aerospace - News - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redwood Class visit Bristol Aerospace
Redwood Class had a blast during their trip to Bristol Aerospace!
Redwood Class pupils visited Bristol Aerospace this June following previous learning about forces in science.
We were lucky enough to visit the concorde hanger by ourselves for the first part of the day. Pupils particularly enjoyed going on the concorde itself and couldn't believe how big it was! There were lots of questions about how the nose of the plane worked!
Following this, we were able to witness an old plane being restored in a neigbouring hanger and one of the engineers workign on the plane was kind enough to explain about the history of the plane and the restorations his team were making. We also explored the main Aerospace museum; particularly enjoying the interactive elements.
We then enjoyed an Engineers of the Future workshop led by Aerospace staff: learning about the history of flight with a focus on Bristol’s most famous aeroplanes. We explored how the materials used to build aeroplanes have changed over time, aerodynamics and the science behind aeroplane design. Pupils then created and tested their own gliders.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bratton Brass Band Visit - News - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Bratton Brass Band Visit
Bratton Brass Band visits Chapmanslade for 'Proms on the Playground'
We were lucky enough to recieve a visit (for the third year running) from Bratton Brass Band.
Our pupils love this visit, where they not only get to listen to some fantastic brass music, but also discover facts about the instruments and even get the chance to have a go!
Our favourite song was George Ezra's 'Shotgun'!

pageCache.pageTitle: Redwood Sponsored Walk - News - Chapmanslade C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redwood Sponsored Walk
Our Year 5s and 6s joined the local Acorn Education Trust schools as part of a 4 mile sponsored walk in Warminster.
The weather was glorious for late September! Redwood Class pupils showed great resilience and had a lot of fun on the day.
Thank you to the Acorn Advantage for making the day possible and to all of the Kingdown School 6th Form helpers who looked after us, cheered us on and guided us on the route.
